title: Al-Haqqah 69:37-44 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Haqqah; noon and meem recap and when letters meet
source: Written for quran/y8 lesson 19 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-Haqqah 69:37-44 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 19. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: لَّا يَأْكُلُهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱلْخَٰطِـُٔونَ (٣٧) فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُونَ (٣٨) وَمَا لَا تُبْصِرُونَ (٣٩) إِنَّهُۥ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍۢ كَرِيمٍۢ (٤٠) وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍۢ ۚ قَلِيلًۭا مَّا تُؤْمِنُونَ (٤١) وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍۢ ۚ قَلِيلًۭا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ (٤٢) تَنزِيلٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ (٤٣) وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنَا بَعْضَ ٱلْأَقَاوِيلِ (٤٤)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: None will eat it except the sinners.
So I swear by what you see
And what you do not see
[That] indeed, the Qur'an is the word of a noble Messenger.
And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe.
Nor the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember.
[It is] a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
And if Muhammad had made up about Us some [false] sayings,

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Haqqah 69:37-44 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 69:37-44 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 69:37-44 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: In the portal box, explain in two sentences why the Qur'an cannot be poetry.
questions.a: Its words are from Allah, revealed to the Prophet ﷺ; it does not follow the poets' metres or their aims.

questions.q: Count the noon sakinah and tanween rules in 69:40 to 43.
questions.a: رَسُولٍۢ كَرِيمٍۢ ikhfa; شَاعِرٍۢ قَلِيلًۭا ikhfa; قَلِيلًۭا مَّا idgham (twice); كَاهِنٍۢ قَلِيلًۭا ikhfa; تَنزِيلٌۭ ikhfa and idgham; مِّن رَّبِّ idgham.

questions.q: 69:41 to 42 say the Qur'an is NOT the word of ...
questions.a: A) a poet or a soothsayer. 69:41 to 42 deny poet and soothsayer; 69:40 and 43 affirm the noble Messenger and the Lord of the worlds.

questions.q: Al-Haqqah 69:43: «تَنزِيلٌۭ مِّن ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Some said the Qur'an was poetry or fortune-telling. Why do you think 69:40 to 43 insist it is 'a revelation from the Lord of the worlds'?
questions.a: To answer those claims: it is the word of a noble Messenger, revealed by Allah, not poetry or soothsaying (69:41 to 43).
